evidence: Source-only review of all 156 criterion descriptions (145 Functional, 4 Polish, 5 Visual, and 2 gates) found no instance that enumerates a full-credit outcome and then waives its own required observations. Workbook Quality Checks row 34 / check 33 and quality-checks.md:138-140 require one full-credit bar; the internal row-34 annotation permits shared flow setup, while current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires preserving independently useful outcomes. Concrete potentially confusing cases were checked against that policy: (1) Frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:551 requires successful revisions that actually save changed nonzero relocation inputs and no relocation settlement; the independent-control fallback removes unrelated second-generation lineage setup, not the successful-change or no-posting bar. (2) functional/judge.toml:1136 starts with artifacts "actually obtained" and requires each existing original artifact to remain unchanged after later actions. Its exclusion of initial artifact creation consistently scopes historical preservation; initial batch receipt, member text and snapshots are separately stated at lines 1109, 1118 and 1127. functional/prompt.md:11 denies unobserved credit, so absence of every preservation witness does not establish this outcome. (3) functional/judge.toml:677 states a conditional imported-DRAFT bar from the outset; its no-import branch matches instruction.md:11 and hireops_rules.md:91-95, rather than waiving a mandatory import. (4) polish/judge.toml:32 permits editable controls or a read-only retained-date confirmation, but both require visible retained effective date and successful retry with that same date. Its alternate genuinely invalid-input witness retains the same recovery outcome, and unavailable interception is explicitly missing evidence. (5) visual/judge.toml:84-89 scopes component consistency and defines one score-5 anchor; separately owned typography/palette/spacing defects are not contradictory alternate full-credit standards. Each other Visual criterion likewise has a single explicit score-5 anchor. Gate exclusions consistently leave advanced economics to scored outcomes (gates/constraints/judge.toml:23-26; gates/render/judge.toml:23). Evidence integrity: raw-evidence-index.json SHA256 1ef29f836bb775ef2ed19fc158bee979aef4d43ead0578fdb13fe9bacb6daad1 matches the assigned input and all 292 listed artifact hashes checked successfully. local/configured-inspection.log SHA256 0033f03c91c8bd03db1d3718a8b9741eb03cb22d0f251700ef3d2d9e039cf4ed explicitly reports parser/prompt/schema/argument-launch observations only; all 15 logged tests source hashes match the frozen candidate, and its criterion counts agree with independent TOML enumeration. Those observations do not establish semantic correctness by themselves; the verdict comes from reading the descriptions. No runtime measurement is necessary for this source self-consistency row. Full configured judge, workload, reward-comparison, Oracle and target-model evidence remains absent and is not waived or represented as measured here.
counterexample: Attempted broken-app case: an app whose revision handler saves nothing and emits no relocation payment cannot earn hro_relocation_revision under functional/judge.toml:551 because successful saved changed relocation inputs are explicit requirements, including for fallback controls. An app that rewrites an earlier batch receipt after a later revision cannot earn hro_change_history under line 1136 merely because other artifact families were initially missing; every existing original artifact must stay unchanged. Attempted conforming alternatives: an app omitting optional demonstration DRAFTs satisfies the explicit conditional bar at line 677, supported by instruction.md:11; a rescission UI retaining the effective date in a read-only confirmation with Retry satisfies polish/judge.toml:32. Neither is falsely excluded by a second competing bar. These are source-based counterexample analyses, not executed app variants.
